Verdict: BENIGN — @whyshu/argent-engine 0.7.6
Sample SHA-256: 3bcdbaa4a33cea0604584e07116bf46467dbba04b87dc6de0858fff1109b0f9a

Release evidence
Fetched registry tarballs 0.7.5 and 0.7.3 and verified their SHA-1 against the
npm packument. SHA-256:
0.7.5 b77e9e83fccbf0dd3fd49f8499f816e26973de54e1a00c22f8509a3af39e3367
0.7.3 3f59d3df735774bbdf7ebf0dc3ea3749585e666d33a6510c30776313b75083b0

Both 0.7.5 and 0.7.6 contain 352 files, with no added/deleted members. Exactly
eight files differ: package.json, MANIFEST.json, engine/VERSION,
engine/version.mjs, appointment-create.mjs, appointment_grab.py,
release-argent.sh, and the appointment skill instructions. The code adds
notification-group resolution from configured gateway JSON, refuses creation
without a notification destination, introduces a dry-run return before secret
access or POST, rejects non-Mexico booking stores, and disables legacy /dl
publishing unless explicitly enabled. The other differences are version,
manifest hash, and corresponding documentation updates. None introduces an
unrelated payload, credential collector, or concealed destination.

Both flagged files, argent-runner.mjs and daily-report.mjs, are byte-identical
to 0.7.5. Compared with the previously reviewed benign 0.7.3, the runner is a
new configured job executor; daily-report gains ERP report publication.
init-ml.sh is byte-identical across 0.7.3, 0.7.5, and 0.7.6.

Execution paths
The runner explicitly loads its configuration, requires serverUrl, tenantAppId
and runnerToken, and restricts the task-board URL to a loopback hostname.
runOnce() claims a job, executeJob() creates/runs/polls a local task-board task,
and completion sends outcome, summary and session reference. serverHeaders()
puts runnerToken in Authorization. No reviewed request body serializes cfg,
runnerToken, or process.env. This is the engine's advertised task dispatch.

main() in daily-report builds selected sales/stock/comparison report fields.
Dry-run and JSON-output paths return before publication. The optional ERP
publisher obtains DAILY_REPORT_BRIDGE_SECRET or the configured local secret
file and sends it in x-appointment-secret; the body is
JSON.stringify({reportDate: payload.date, payload}). The env helper parameter
is not serialized. buildReportPayload() selects business fields rather than
spreading the OAuth store record. Neither flagged flow establishes theft.

Cleave facts reports source-local secret-http-body candidates for both files,
including module-level summary events, with flow limitation flags. These are
approximate provenance leads, refuted as credential-body claims by tracing
the actual arguments and header construction. There is no encoded executable
layer in these two source files. No package entrypoint was executed.

Dependency lead
The exact listed Playwright 1.64.0 macOS wheel was fetched from files.pythonhosted.org.
Its SHA-256 matches both the supplied dependency checksum and PyPI metadata:
d76a501c9930b5a097b00e2448cda2200122a1e8e4be762ff535c1b076277737
The unchanged setup script explicitly installs playwright into its venv, first
using its configured package mirror and then the default index. The Python
entrypoint computes the bundled Node/cli.js path and invokes it with the user
arguments and driver environment. The core bundle implements browser process
launch/stdio/temporary-directory cleanup, browser download selection, proxying
and automation transport. Large bundles and a bundled Node runtime explain
the capability volume. The unchanged install command supplies no dependency
substitution evidence in this release. The wheel scan has no suspicious or
hostile findings; large-file flow limitations remain explicit.

Trait changes
The credential-env HTTP candidate retains exactly its previous matcher and
exceptions, with notable severity and a description acknowledging may-flow.
Its predicates do not distinguish header authentication from disclosure.
Exfiltration consumers now require the existing explicit credential-environment
body evidence rather than treating the generic candidate as collection.
No package name, vendor hostname, or sample-specific exclusion was added.

The neutral-observation-moves.json ledger records misplaced source, stream,
module-import and launchd facts moved out of objective categories. Matchers,
platforms, type scope and exact consumers are preserved, except that the two
address-named loop fragments and their sole aggregate are consolidated into
the aggregate's exact regex union. Merely naming a loop variable ip/host/addr
does not establish scanning. Bare hex-array entries in check-sample-redaction
are truncated token hashes, not encoded payloads. The telemetry import names
a shipped helper, not Python startup persistence. LaunchAgent path/configuration
facts establish service configuration, not unwanted reactivation.

Supporting placement repairs move actual Node stdio .pipe calls to stream I/O,
a bare 1023/1024 token to source shape, and an embedded-code source metric to
source shape. These preserve their matchers and exact consumers and keep all
leaves within their existing reviewed budgets. Whole-objective ancestor
selectors deliberately stop inheriting these neutral observations: in the
reviewed consumers they serve attack-context or attack-exclusion roles, and
ordinary source syntax, a numeric token, or configuration supplies neither.
New neutral ancestor membership was audited for threshold/proximity effects.
The sole remaining package objective, runtime/host profiling, requires three
actual host-query capabilities and accurately describes the bundled telemetry.

Verification
atomscan and cleave facts ran on the supplied archive, the two flagged members,
and the exact dependency wheel. The updated archive JSON contains 353 units
and zero suspicious/hostile traits. The seven existing Argent controls pass.
check-neutral-observations.py adds 22 positive/near-miss placement checks,
header-only authentication, aliased credentials and explicit credential JSON;
credential-body evidence remains suspicious. The move ledger also updates
existing source-metric and 1024-token consumers and fixture expectations.
The final repository check is make validate, run after all edits and the
single judgement marker are complete.
